headline: Yields stopped going up and it didn't matter — the dollar took the baton, breaking Europe, Mexico and EM while US semis levitated and the 30-year mortgage printed 7.28%.
summary: The rates shock paused: the curve held at 52-week highs (30y 5.64%, 10y 5.29%, 5y 5.09%, all at the 100th percentile) without extending, MOVE finally ticked down 1.1% to 109.28, and TLT (+0.3%) and IEF (+0.1%) eked out gains. The rates composite improved only marginally to -82. Pause, not repair: MOVE is still +40.3% on the month with z=2.19 and acceleration 1.65, the 10y real yield is 2.93% (+49bp on the month, acc 1.54), and the pass-through to the real economy arrived today anyway — the 30-year mortgage printed 7.28%, +25bp in a week and +62bp in a month, z=1.85, at the top of its 52-week range. That is the number that matters for Q4 earnings in housing and consumer credit, and it lands with ITB -4.9% on the month at the 6th percentile, XHB/SPY at the 2nd percentile, HD -11.1% on the month at the 0th percentile, and MCD -11.3% (z=-2.41).

What changed today is the dollar. DXY +0.7% to 102.16 — 100th percentile, z=1.24, acceleration 1.00, turning up — and the damage was all offshore. EURUSD -1.0% to 1.1231, 0th percentile of the year. USDMXN +1.8% to 18.368: z=3.07 with acceleration 2.48, the single most extreme series on the board, up from z=2.30 yesterday. USDCAD z=1.62/acc 1.51, AUDUSD -0.9%, CEW -0.4%. Equities paid instantly: Euro Stoxx -1.5%, CAC -1.6%, FTSE -1.7%, EWI -2.7%, EWP -2.2%, EWG -1.2%, EWW -2.7%, GREK -2.5%, EPOL -2.4%, ARGT -2.0%, EZA -1.7%, TUR -13.4% on the month. EFA/SPY fell another 1.1% and sits at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks. Yesterday's story was a domestic rates accident; today it's a global funding squeeze, and the dollar composite at -22 understates how one-sided the move has become.

Underneath, the US barbell got narrower, not wider. SPX +0.2% to 7,663.7 and NDX +0.3% were entirely a semis story: SMH +1.3% (+13.2% on the month, rel +12.6%), SOXX +15.1% on the month, SMH/SPY z=1.71 with acceleration 1.48, AMD +34.1% on the month and 65% above its 200-day, MU +14.8%, TSM +10.9%, CIBR +8.0%. High beta / low vol made a new 52-week high (+12.6% on the month). Against that, credit kept bleeding — HYG -0.4% to 76.90, z=-1.74 with acceleration -1.23 and a rolling_over trend, LQD -3.0% on the month at the 0th percentile, HYG/IEF -0.5% — and the capital-markets complex is in open liquidation: XLF -6.5% on the month (rel -6.9%) despite 3m10y at the 100th percentile, BX -18.1% (z=-1.87, acc -1.59), GS -10.7%, IAI -7.9%, KIE -6.2%. Breadth bounced cosmetically (RSP/SPY +0.2%, IWM +0.6%, MDY +0.9%) but RSP/SPY still carries z=-1.94 at the 7th percentile. Hedges got marginally more expensive and are still absurd: VIX 16.84 at the 19th percentile, VIX3M 18.80 at the 12th, term structure 0.896 turning up.

Two calls from yesterday need marking. The gold-miner re-bid failed outright: gold +0.4% to 4,201 but GDX -0.3% (-5.2% on the week) with acceleration -2.44, GDXJ acc -2.24, GDX/GOLD acc -2.59, NEM acc -2.39 — the debasement hedge is being sold into a firm dollar, and the whole hard-asset complex went with it (XME -10.0% on the month, REMX -2.2% today and -17.5% on the month at the 1st percentile, NLR -11.1% at the 0th percentile). And the crude "relief" split: WTI +1.9% to 92.14 while Brent -2.1% to 101.33 and gasoline -1.9%, with XLE +1.2% and XOP +1.9% — energy equities bid, inflation composite still -34. The offsets that remain are real: growth pulse +18, copper 6.557 holding +7.2% on the quarter with copper/gold at the 93rd percentile (acc 1.11), electrification turning up hard (GEV +4.5% today, +10.6% on the month, acc 1.07; ETN +11.5% on the month, acc 1.49; CAT +2.0%), and the crypto complex flipping to turning_up across the board (BTC +9.4%, ETH +11.6%, SOL +18.3%, MSTR +27.9% on the month). Risk regime -14. This is still not a growth scare — it's a dollar and term-premium squeeze that is now exporting itself.

good.text: Bond vol stopped going up for the first time in weeks: MOVE -1.1% to 109.28, with TLT +0.3% and IEF +0.1% and the curve holding rather than extending. Rates composite improved to -82.
Semis remain the only clean uptrend: SMH +1.3% (+13.2% 1m, rel +12.6%), SOXX +15.1% on the month, SMH/SPY z=1.71 with acceleration 1.48, TSM +10.9%, AMD +34.1%, MU +14.8%, CIBR +8.0%.

No demand recession in the cyclical tape: growth pulse +18, copper 6.557 (+7.2% 3m), copper/gold at the 93rd percentile with acceleration 1.11, industrials/utilities +4.5% on the month, high-beta/low-vol at a 52-week high.

The electrification trade turned back up while the nuclear/power-IPP leg stayed broken: GEV +4.5% today and +10.6% on the month (acc 1.07), ETN +11.5% on the month (acc 1.49), CAT +2.0%, GRID turning up.

Crypto flipped to turning_up across the complex with the dollar rising — BTC +1.4% to 84,700 (+9.4% 1m, +37.8% 3m), ETH +11.6%, SOL +18.3%, MSTR +4.4% today and +27.9% on the month, and all still only in the 28th-40th percentile of the past year.
Small and mid caps actually led the index today: MDY +0.9%, IWM +0.6%, IWM/SPY +0.5%, RSP/SPY +0.2% — a first flicker of internal repair, though off a 7th-percentile base.

bad.text: The 30-year mortgage printed 7.28%: +25bp in a week, +62bp in a month, z=1.85, 100th percentile. Housing transmission is now mechanical — ITB -4.9% on the month at the 6th percentile, XHB/SPY at the 2nd, DHI -3.7%, HD -11.1% at the 0th percentile.

Dollar breakout, and it is accelerating: DXY +0.7% to 102.16 at the 100th percentile (acc 1.00), EURUSD -1.0% at the 0th percentile, USDMXN z=3.07 with acceleration 2.48, USDCAD z=1.62/acc 1.51, AUDUSD -0.9%, EM FX basket -0.4%.

Everything priced in a non-dollar currency broke: Euro Stoxx -1.5%, CAC -1.6%, FTSE -1.7%, EWI -2.7%, EWP -2.2%, EWW -2.7%, GREK -2.5%, EPOL -2.4%, EZA -1.7%. EFA/SPY -1.1% and sitting at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks.

Credit kept paying the bill: HYG -0.4% to 76.90, z=-1.74 with acceleration -1.23 and rolling over, LQD -3.0% on the month at the 0th percentile, HYG/IEF -0.5%. The ratio still looks fine only because Treasuries are falling too.

The capital-markets complex is in liquidation despite the steepest 3m10y in a year: XLF -6.5% on the month (z=-1.54, rel -6.9%), BX -18.1% (z=-1.87, acc -1.59), GS -10.7%, IAI -7.9%, KIE -6.2%, KBE -5.1%.

The debasement hedge failed on a firm dollar: gold +0.4% but GDX -0.3% (-5.2% on the week, acc -2.44), GDX/GOLD acceleration -2.59, NEM acc -2.39. The wider hard-asset unwind continues — XME -10.0% on the month, REMX -17.5% at the 1st percentile, NLR -11.1% at the 0th.

trades.name: Short developed ex-US vs long S&P
trades.line: Short EFA vs long SPY: dollar squeeze is breaking DM ex-US
trades.expr: Sell EFA against an equal-notional long in SPY (or short EWG/EWU/EWI basket vs SPY if you want the Europe-only cut).
trades.thesis: A 100th-percentile dollar is a direct earnings and flow tax on unhedged DM ex-US equity. The US index has semis to offset it; Europe has nothing — XLF-equivalent banks and exporters are the whole index and both are hostage to EUR and global funding.
trades.trigger: DXY +0.7% to 102.16 (acc 1.00, 100th pctile) with EURUSD -1.0% to 1.1231 at the 0th percentile; EFA -1.0% vs SPY +0.1% today; EFA/SPY -1.1% on the day, -3.9% on the month, z=-1.23, 0th percentile of 52 weeks and 5.1% below its 200-day. Euro Stoxx -1.5%, CAC -1.6%, EWI -2.7%.
trades.stop: EFA/SPY reclaiming its 200-day, or DXY's 1-month z-score falling back below 0.5 with EURUSD off its 52-week low.
trades.target: Another 4-5% on the ratio; EFA/SPY stays pinned in the bottom decile through the quarter.

trades.name: Short Mexico equity (EWW) / long USDMXN
trades.line: Short EWW: peso at 3-sigma break, Mexico index rolling over
trades.expr: Short EWW outright or buy 2-3 month EWW puts; FX version is long USD/MXN via CME MXN futures.
trades.thesis: The peso was the last high-carry EM currency still holding; it has now broken with the most extreme momentum reading on the board. Local equity in dollar terms takes both the FX hit and the risk-premium hit, and the local index is already rolling over in pesos.
trades.trigger: USDMXN +1.8% today to 18.368: +8.1% on the month, z=3.07, acceleration 2.48, 5.4% above its 200-day — up from z=2.30 yesterday. EWW -2.7% today, -8.6% on the month, relative strength -9.0%; MXX -1.3% and rolling over; EM FX basket CEW -0.4%.
trades.stop: USDMXN closing back below its 200-day or the 1-month z dropping under 1.5; EWW reclaiming its 200-day (currently 7.9% above spot).
trades.target: Another 7-8% lower in EWW, matching the 3-month -8.4% run; USDMXN extension of the 1-month +8.1%.

trades.name: Short US housing (ITB)
trades.line: Short ITB: 7.28% mortgage, +62bp in a month, no bid
trades.expr: Short ITB or buy Jan ITB puts; single-name expression DHI short, consumer read-through HD.
trades.thesis: The mortgage rate is the cleanest transmission channel from the term-premium shock to earnings, and it just made a fresh high. Order books, cancellations and incentive costs follow with a one-quarter lag; the group has not yet discounted a 7-handle sustained.
trades.trigger: MORTGAGE30US 7.28% today: +25bp on the week, +62bp on the month, z=1.85, 100th percentile, 13.5% above its 200-day. ITB -4.9% on the month, -14.6% on the quarter, 6th percentile, 9.7% below its 200-day; XHB/SPY at the 2nd percentile; HD -11.1% on the month at the 0th percentile; DHI -13.9% on the quarter.
trades.stop: Mortgage rate's 1-month change turning negative alongside the 10y breaking its up-trend, or ITB closing back above its 200-day.
trades.target: Another 8-10% in ITB; XHB/SPY holding the bottom 2% of its range.

trades.name: Long equity vol against cheap spot
trades.line: Long vol: VIX 16.8 vs breadth at 7th pctile, MOVE z=2.2
trades.expr: Buy 1-3 month SPX put spreads ~5% OTM funded by selling further-OTM puts, or VIX call spreads; roll on term-structure inversion.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced in the bottom fifth of its year against bond vol in the top decile and breadth in the bottom tenth. Every prior episode of this gap closed through equity vol, not through bond vol falling. You are being paid to own the convexity rather than to predict the catalyst.
trades.trigger: VIX +3.1% to 16.84 (19th pctile) and VIX3M +2.3% to 18.80 (12th pctile), with the term structure 0.896 turning up. Against that: MOVE 109.28, +40.3% on the month, z=2.19, acceleration 1.65; RSP/SPY z=-1.94 at the 7th percentile; HYG z=-1.74 with acceleration -1.23; SKEW -4.5% on the month means tail hedges also cheapened.
trades.stop: VIX3M making new 52-week lows while RSP/SPY z recovers above -1 and HYG stops rolling over — i.e. internals confirm the index.
trades.target: VIX into the low-20s / term structure above 1.00; a 1.5-2x on the put spread.

trades.name: Long semis vs short financials
trades.line: Long SMH vs short XLF: the only trend that still pays
trades.expr: Long SMH (or SOXX) against an equal-notional short in XLF; add BX or GS to the short leg for higher beta to the capital-markets unwind.
trades.thesis: Financials are failing to monetise the steepest curve in a year, which means the market is pricing credit and capital-markets revenue risk, not NIM. Semis are the one group with accelerating relative strength and an actual order cycle. Own the momentum, fund it with the broken cyclical.
trades.trigger: SMH +1.3% today, +13.2% on the month, relative strength +12.6%, SMH/SPY z=1.71 with acceleration 1.48; SOXX +15.1% on the month. XLF -6.5% on the month, z=-1.54, relative strength -6.9%, rolling over despite 3m10y at 1.09 and the 100th percentile; BX -18.1% on the month (acc -1.59), GS -10.7%, IAI -7.9%.
trades.stop: SMH is 23.7% above its 200-day — if SMH/SPY z falls back below 0 or XLF relative strength turns up, the pair is done. Hard stop on a 6% adverse move in the spread.
trades.target: Another 8-10% on the pair over the quarter; SMH/SPY back toward its 52-week high.

trades.name: Long loans vs short high yield
trades.line: Long BKLN vs short HYG: own the carry, not the duration
trades.expr: Long BKLN against an equal-notional short HYG; size 1:1 since HYG carries roughly 3-4 years more duration.
trades.thesis: This is the cleanest way to be short the credit crack without being short carry. Loans float off a 4.20% front end that isn't moving; HY bonds eat the entire 54bp monthly move in the 10y plus widening spreads. If credit is genuinely rolling over, HYG underperforms twice.
trades.trigger: HYG -0.4% today to 76.90, -2.8% on the month, z=-1.74 with acceleration -1.23 and a rolling_over trend; LQD -3.0% on the month at the 0th percentile. BKLN flat on the month, +2.1% on the quarter, 87th percentile, 1.9% above its 200-day. 3m bill 4.20% (+29bp on the month) keeps the loan coupon high while 10y at 5.29% kills the bond.
trades.stop: HYG's 1-month z recovering above 0 with HYG/IEF breaking to new highs on spread tightening rather than Treasury weakness; or BKLN breaking its 200-day (loan credit losses arriving first).
trades.target: 3-4% of relative performance over the quarter.

trades.name: Long bitcoin exposure (IBIT)
trades.line: Long IBIT: whole crypto complex flipped to turning_up
trades.expr: Long IBIT; higher-beta sleeve via MSTR, which is leading. Keep size small — this is the one long that fights the dollar.
trades.thesis: A rising-dollar, rising-real-yield tape should be killing crypto and isn't — the complex turned up simultaneously across spot, alts and equities while gold miners broke. That divergence usually marks the start of a flows cycle, and positioning is nowhere near crowded with BTC still 28.6% lower year-on-year.
trades.trigger: BTC +1.4% to 84,700, +9.4% on the month, +37.8% on the quarter, trend turning_up and 14.6% above its 200-day; ETH +11.6% and SOL +18.3% on the month with ETH/BTC turning up; MSTR +4.4% today and +27.9% on the month; IBIT +9.6% on the month yet only at the 39th percentile of its 52-week range.
trades.stop: BTC closing back below its 200-day, or MSTR's relative strength turning down — the equity proxies crack first.
trades.target: Retrace toward the upper half of the 52-week range, roughly 15-20% in IBIT.
